title: Jeden dzień · koniec
note: B1 CAPSTONE — same genre as a2_wrapup_func (ZERO new material, situation_chunk recombination, teaches_lemmas empty). tree.json's own node note names four registers to recombine: narrative, plans, politeness, opinions. Built the whole unit strictly from those four source units' own teaches_lemmas -- b1_plans (planuję, spotkanie, termin, w przyszłym tygodniu, muszę, załatwić), b1_polite (przepraszam, że przeszkadzam, czy mógłby pan mi pomóc, nie ma problemu -- all copied verbatim as whole chunks), b1_stories (najpierw, nagle) plus b1_journeys for the narrative payload itself (szedłem from b1_past_isc, zgubiłem się and the exact taught frame spóźniłem się do pracy from b1_journeys -- do+Gen, not na+Acc, checked against that pack's own sentences before use so as not to invent an ungoverned frame), and b1_opinions (moim zdaniem, zgadzam się, na pewno). DELIBERATE SCOPE: b1_vocative_chunks was considered for a fifth register (an address form somewhere in the narrative) and dropped -- the node note names exactly four registers and stacking a fifth risked diluting the discrimination drill the way a2_wrapup_func's own five-situations mix never tried to add a sixth. TITLE: tree.json's placeholder used the raw level code 'B1' in the Polish title field; changed to 'Jeden dzień, koniec' (both words taught: dzień trunk_social_a1, koniec leaf_ideas_a1) -- a level code is not Polish vocabulary and putting one in a learner-visible Polish title read as the same class of problem the AGENTS title rule already bans, even though it isn't literally an untaught inflected form. title_en kept as 'B1 capstone', matching a2_wrapup_func's own English title being allowed to name the level informally. Every recombined sentence checked individually against check_new.py before writing: rejected as NEW and never used -- wycieczkę (accusative of wycieczka, only the nominative is taught), zadzwonić, jechałem/jechał (no taught past of jechać, only its present), pomógł/pomagał/pomagali (no taught past of pomóc or pomagać -- b1_dative_sg only ever taught pomagać's present tense), długi, powtórzy, poszedłem (a THIRD prefix on iść's past stem beyond the two b1_arrive_leave taught -- przyszedłem/wyszedłem only, po- was never taught and would be a silent new-prefix leak). 'Planuję spotkanie' relies on neuter Acc=Nom needing no new form (spotkanie is unchanged in both jobs) -- same standing pattern as 'Kupiłem chleb' (masc inanimate, also unchanged) already used repeatedly since a2_aspect; not a new fact, just a recognised pattern applied to a different noun. Quiz built entirely as discrimination across the same twelve already-taught chunks (never introduces a thirteenth string) -- matches a2_wrapup_func's own convention of testing which SITUATION a look-alike-shaped phrase belongs to, not testing new recall.

intro.title: One day, nothing new
intro.body:
This unit closes B1, and it teaches you no new Polish at all. Every phrase in it you already own — from planning something, being polite when you need help, telling a short story about your day, and saying what you think about it.

Up to now each register was practised on its own. Here they're chained together into one ordinary day: you plan something, something goes wrong on the way, you politely ask for help, and at the end you say what you thought of it.
intro.body_pl: Planuję… Przepraszam, że przeszkadzam… Najpierw… Moim zdaniem…

intro.title: Four registers, one shape each
intro.body: A plan states an intention (Planuję…, Muszę…). A polite request softens a demand (Czy mógłby…?, Przepraszam, że…). A narrative connective moves a story forward in time (Najpierw…, Nagle…). An opinion frames a judgement (Moim zdaniem…, Na pewno…). None of these four shapes overlap — but until you've mixed them into one scene, it's easy to reach for the wrong one out of habit.
intro.body_pl: Planuję… · Czy mógłby…? · Najpierw… · Moim zdaniem…

rows: Moim zdaniem to był zły dzień.

intro.title: A whole day, four registers
intro.body: Here is the whole thing chained together — a plan, a story that goes wrong, a polite request, and an opinion at the end. Nothing in it is new; every sentence is a chunk from one of the four units you already finished. Read it once as a story before you start the exercises.
intro.body_pl: Planuję spotkanie w przyszłym tygodniu. Najpierw szedłem do banku. Nagle zgubiłem się. Spóźniłem się do pracy. Przepraszam, że przeszkadzam — czy mógłby pan mi pomóc? Nie ma problemu. Moim zdaniem to był zły dzień. Zgadzam się.

examples.en: Plan: I'm planning a meeting next week.
Story: I was late for work.

match.en: We have an appointment next week.
I have to sort it out.
First I was going to the bank.

quiz.prompt: A colleague asks if you're free next week. You say:
quiz.explain: The next-week detail is the specific answer to the question — the other three are all true statements that don't actually answer it.

quiz.prompt: You're mid-conversation and need to interrupt politely. You say:
quiz.explain: This chunk is built for exactly one job — softening an interruption. Muszę to załatwić states an intention, it doesn't open a conversation.

quiz.prompt: You need a stranger's help with something. You say:
choices: Moim zdaniem to był zły dzień.
quiz.explain: mógłby softens the request into a real question, not a demand.

quiz.prompt: Someone apologises for a small mistake. You reassure them:
quiz.explain: Nie ma problemu closes the matter. Muszę to załatwić would mean the opposite — that something still needs doing.

quiz.prompt: You're telling a friend what happened on your way to work, in order. You start with:
quiz.explain: Najpierw opens a sequence — it has to come first in a story, not in a plan or an opinion.

quiz.prompt: Something unexpected interrupts your story. You say:
quiz.explain: Nagle marks the turn in a narrative. Na pewno is an opinion word, not a story connective.

quiz.prompt: You explain why you weren't on time. You say:
choices: Moim zdaniem to był zły dzień.
quiz.explain: This is the one sentence that actually names being late — the others are a plan, an opinion, and a request.

quiz.prompt: A friend asks what you thought of the day. You say:
choices: Moim zdaniem to był zły dzień.
quiz.answer: Moim zdaniem to był zły dzień.
quiz.explain: Moim zdaniem frames a judgement — none of the other three do.

quiz.prompt: A friend shares an opinion and you feel the same. You say:
quiz.explain: Zgadzam się responds to someone else's opinion. Nie ma problemu responds to an apology, not an opinion — a different job even though both sound reassuring.

quiz.prompt: You're confident something will happen. You say:
quiz.explain: Na pewno states certainty about the future. Planuję spotkanie only states an intention — it doesn't promise anything will actually happen.

Type the whole day: I'm planning a meeting next week. First I was going to the bank. Suddenly I got lost. I was late for work. Sorry to bother you — could you help me, sir? It's no problem. In my opinion, it was a bad day. I agree.
